description: Earliest known concept/build in the Alfr3d lineage.
Early 2014 iteration of the home-automation daemon.
2014 iteration, ordering relative to MK-I/MK-II unconfirmed.
Home-automation daemon running on a Pi (/home/alfr3d/alfr3ddaemon.py), audio handling.
Added Python LIFX integration (pylifx).
Server + mobile companion apps split out: Alfr3dServer, Alfr3d4Android-Original, Alfr3d-MKIII-Android, alfr3d.io.
Separate repo from the 2015 MK-IV Notion page, not yet reconciled with it.
Repo explicitly describes itself as "Successor to Project Alfr3d" — a rebrand attempt that didn't end up replacing it. Undated.
First Kafka message-bus architecture (topics speak/environment/device/user); direct architectural precursor to today's Kafka-based backend. Undated.

milestone: Backend v0.2.0: Auth, secrets, IoT & reliability hardening
description: Consolidated into today's Littl3-1-Engineering/alfr3d repo and shipped v0.1.8 through v0.2.0 in one sprint: full JWT Auth + RBAC across all 56 write routes with a household login UI, Fernet-encrypted integration secrets at rest, ESPHome as a new local-only IoT provider (mDNS discovery, Noise-encrypted API), and a device-registry-backed multi-camera streaming model. Also landed real production fixes along the way: a stalled-ffmpeg self-heal for camera streams, systemd autostart so all 12 containers survive a reboot unattended, owner-role user management with self-service profile editing, centralized IoT device control, first-run onboarding (account claim + owner generation), and a calendar name-trim/UTC-normalization fix. Also shipped: a Mermaid ER diagram of the live MySQL schema in the README, a now-playing Spotify endpoint (GET /api/music/now-playing) feeding a situational-awareness card, and a mood/genre recommendation resolver that deep-links to a real Spotify playlist. A late-sprint gap surfaced and closed: two services (the daemon and the speak/TTS service) were left out of the secrets-at-rest volume wiring, logging repeated permission errors until both were wired in.

milestone: Nexus Launcher: v0.1.33, Custom Colors, rotation lock & write-action sign-in
description: Free spatial launcher with a $5.99 Pro unlock went live, with CI building a debug APK on every push and a signed-release workflow on version tags (code and latest cut tag both now at v0.1.33). Since then: user-defined Custom Colors theming via an in-app HSV picker, a Behavior-settings rotation-lock toggle that keeps the launcher upright in portrait regardless of device orientation, Keystore-backed sign-in gating for ALFR3D write actions, pinning the NUC's self-signed HTTPS cert, a shared App Drawer/Quick Search app-search cache, an Ambient Brief "Play it" deep-link into the resolved Spotify playlist recommendation, and (2026-08-27) calendar events with a destination now hand off straight to the device's default maps app, replacing a Google Maps Directions dependency that needed a paid tier the household never actually configured.

milestone: littl31.com: site launch + copy & scroll-reveal fixes
description: Product site for Littl3.1 Engineering went live (index, alfr3d, lab pages), followed by real descriptive copy on the alfr3d.html product cards and a round of bug fixes: a Locomotive Scroll init crash that was silently blocking all scroll-reveal content sitewide, a stale scroll-trigger position after async image loads, a card layout restructure, and a ReferenceError in the splash logo animation caused by a mis-scoped easing closure.

milestone: Pricing strategy: monetization plan → Kit-first → 3 SKUs
description: Published the core monetization plan (Core free / Launcher free+Pro / Cloud / Kit), then revised it twice: first to a Kit-first ladder with a Butler subscription replacing the old Cloud tiers, then simplified again by cutting the standalone Relay tier — landing on exactly 3 paid SKUs (Nexus Pro, Kit, Butler).
All 3 repos (alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, Littl31) migrated from personal armageddion account to the Littl3-1-Engineering org.

Corrected: repo does have a LICENSE file (FSL-1.1-ALv2 text, matches the site). GitHub's NOASSERTION was a license-detector classification gap for a non-SPDX-standard license, not a missing file. No action needed.

Build one Kit end-to-end and time assembly before publishing the $399 Founding-100 price. Validates ~$252 landed-cost estimate (Pi 5 8GB, NVMe+HAT, PSU, enclosure, cooling, cabling, packaging, assembly labor, shipping, fees, support/DOA reserve) against a real build, not just parts pricing.

milestone: littl31.com commerce: Stripe Checkout + Founding 100 preorder
description: Top GTM priority: pricing page currently has zero CTA/checkout links on either tier. Add Stripe Checkout for the Kit (Founding 100 preorder with published ship-by date) and Relay/Butler signup + Customer Portal.

alfr3d_deck brought up to alfr3d's baseline: pre-commit-hooks (trailing-whitespace/end-of-file/yaml/large-files) + detect-secrets (fresh baseline, one expected finding -- keystore.properties.sample's changeme placeholders), Dependabot for gradle + github-actions. alfr3d_deck already had CI (build.yml, release.yml) -- ahead of alfr3d there, whose own ci.yml is actually .disabled (a stale claim in this todo corrected). littl31 and Aikido (needs external account signup) still open.

milestone: SmartThings generic IoT control endpoint — fixed, pending live-device verification
description: Fixed 2026-08-24, same day it was found: control_iot_device() (routes/iot.py) now has a source=='smartthings' branch using a new st_utils.translate_generic_control_params() that mirrors the HA translator, mapping ControlBlade's generic command vocabulary to an ST (capability, command, args) triple. sync_st_devices() now also derives device_type via a new st_utils.normalize_st_device_type() from the device's capability list, instead of storing ST's raw deviceTypeName label -- confirmed nothing else in the codebase read that raw label. Both pieces are code-complete and committed; still needs verification against a live SmartThings device, which is the only reason this isn't Shipped yet.
Personality panel currently shows call-count usage only; per-token usage metadata from the LLM client isn't surfaced yet. Minor — a future-enhancement aside, not a scoped plan.
Push notifications to the launcher; depends on Alfr3d Cloud Phase 3 shipping first.
Have the launcher push on-device now-playing (any media session, not just Spotify) to the backend instead of only backend-side polling. Documented as a deferred fast-follow, not yet scoped.
Its own todo/ folder was checked directly and contains only a completed bugfix note (mobile scramble jitter fix); no forward-looking roadmap items exist for the site itself.
Abstract audio-source interface so playback isn't Spotify-only — local library, Tidal, YouTube Music, radio — plus a loose future-ideas list (NLU voice control, Last.fm scrobbling, multi-room sync).
Two more theme options for the existing theme-picker system, on top of the three already shipped (Cyan/Navy, Amber/Charcoal, Light/Teal).

Signing, Gradle Play Publisher, and gated CI already wired up; blocked on manual account-holder steps: Play developer enrollment, Play Console app entry, first manual release upload, sensitive-permission declarations + demo video, hosted privacy policy URL, CI service account for future automated releases.
Attribute calendar/Gmail integrations to individual household members instead of one shared global account. Blocked on Auth + RBAC landing first.
Three parked options beyond the already-shipped HLS pipeline: WebRTC for sub-500ms latency, recorded/archived playback, and computer-vision motion/person detection.
Pre-flashed Raspberry Pi appliance, built to order. Parked until Alfr3d Cloud proves demand. Not yet scheduled.

Remote-access relay (no port forwarding) + push notifications; "thin, dumb-pipe relay" that never sees plaintext data. Now scoped into a phased plan in todo_cloud_relay.md: architecture spike -> subscriber/billing identity + Stripe -> relay/tunnel -> FCM push -> security review. Deliberately a separate identity system from household RBAC auth. Not yet built.

milestone: Personality ticks shouldn't fire on every speak
description: Personality quip "ticks" currently apply to every TTS speak action; should be probabilistic/occasional (random chance, cooldown, or context-based) so it doesn't feel like a bit every time. Newly scoped, not started.

Physical enclosure for the ALFR3D device + peripherals (mic/speaker/camera/sensors), matching the dark tactical/glassmorphic visual identity. Not currently scheduled — blocked on the hardware phase starting and a finalized bill of materials.

milestone: Kit ordering / Cloud signup commerce plan
description: Phased plan to give the Kit and Cloud pricing sections a real path from visitor to paying customer — site currently has zero CTA/checkout links on either tier. Phase A: free waitlist/interest-capture forms. Phase B (gated on Kit waitlist signal): Stripe Checkout for the one-time Kit purchase. Phase C (gated on the Cloud relay being built): Stripe Checkout + Customer Portal + magic-link login alongside the relay's own subscriber identity. Planning only, not started.

milestone: Self-awareness: pronounce own name + don't self-greet
description: Both identity bugs fixed 2026-08-27, not yet on-device verified: normalize_pronunciation() in service_speak regex-substitutes the leetspeak "alfr3d" to "Alfred" right before every TTS call, and update_user_state() in service_user now guards the welcome-greeting flow so the alfr3d system user never announces itself coming online like a household member (its presence-state row still updates normally). A closer look also found the guard is currently dead/defensive code -- no code path in the schema seed or the three runtime user-insert sites ever creates a row with username='alfr3d'.

milestone: Hardware pivot: Pi 5 → N100 mini PC, margin restored
description: Switched Kit hardware plan from Raspberry Pi 5 to an N100 mini PC (e.g. Beelink Mini S12 Pro, 8GB/256GB) after the user flagged their own NUC as a cheaper reference point. A DIY mini-ITX build was evaluated and rejected as more expensive than a complete pre-built unit. Mini PC parts total ~$235 CAD vs $425 CAD for the Pi 5 tier, restoring $164-214 margin at $399/$449 pricing.

milestone: CAD BOM correction + revised CAGR/monetization strategy
description: Recommended-tier Kit parts corrected from $191 (a USD-MSRP artifact) to ~$425 CAD verified Canadian pricing -- Founding-100 ($399) now underwater on parts alone before the N100 pivot above. Added a market CAGR range (12-20% working estimate) and a revised pricing/sales plan: budget-tier storage default, Founding-100 reframed as a small hand-assembled batch, Butler subscription as the primary margin engine. Realistic Year 1: 40-100 Kit units; Year 2: 150-400 cumulative.

New situational-awareness card that reads household composition (who's home vs. away, known vs. unknown devices) and surfaces it with urgency-aware styling on the Ambient Brief. Backend check + Deck card both built and unit-tested; not yet verified on-device.

New backend endpoint + routines/now-playing tracking so the launcher can surface a "pick up where you left off" card across surfaces (e.g. resume music paused elsewhere, or a routine edited on the web dashboard). Built and unit-tested; not yet verified on-device.

Learns each device's typical on/off rhythm from history and flags when something is still on well past its usual pattern (e.g. a light on much later than normal). Backend baseline computation + anomaly check built and unit-tested; not yet verified on-device and no real baseline data has accumulated yet.

milestone: Deck: Attention telemetry as a focus signal
description: Launcher reports rolling attention/dwell telemetry to a new backend endpoint, feeding focus and wind-down situational-awareness signals. Built and unit-tested on both sides; not yet verified on-device.
Predict a household member's usual departure time from history and surface it as an Ambient Brief card. Scoped alongside the other new situational-awareness cards; not yet built.

milestone: New feature: departure anomaly detection ("usually gone by now, still home")
description: Companion to rhythm-break anomaly detection: flag when a household member is still home well past when they'd usually have left. Idea only, not scoped.

milestone: Explore: Nexus Launcher as a new context source for Alfr3d
description: Explore feeding the launcher's own on-device signals (attention/dwell, foreground app, etc.) back into the backend's situational-awareness engine as a new context source, alongside existing presence/device signals. Idea only, not scoped.

milestone: Explore free/open-source routing for travel guidance
description: Google Maps Directions (paid tier, never actually configured) was removed 2026-08-27; the launcher's "next event soon" card now just hands off to the device's default maps app with no computed leave-by time or fuel-cost estimate. This explores reviving smarter guidance via a free/self-hostable routing source instead -- candidates: OSRM (self-hosted, MIT, no per-request billing), OpenRouteService, GraphHopper, Valhalla. None offer Google's real-time traffic layer. Exploration only, not started.

milestone: Clean up GitHub CI/CD, security & Aikido CVEs (all repos)
description: CI/CD + security cleanup across all three repos: re-enable alfr3d's disabled ci.yml, finish Aikido signup for littl31, and triage/remediate CVEs Aikido flags once scanning is live across alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, and Littl31. Distinct from Repo tooling standardization (pre-commit/detect-secrets/Dependabot baseline) -- this is the CI pipeline health + vulnerability remediation pass. Not started.
